name: Tattenai
overview: Tattenai is a male governor noted in Scripture for opposing the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem. His role is specifically mentioned in Ezra 5:3, where he challenges the efforts of the Israelites to restore their place of worship. Beyond this, no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Tattenai appears once in Scripture, in Ezra 5:3, with no special meaning or divine origin indicated. It is simply presented as his proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tattenai beyond his official capacity as a governor who opposed the Temple rebuilding. No relatives or personal connections are mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Tattenai's significance lies in his opposition to the Israelites' God-ordained project to rebuild the Temple, reflecting the external challenges faced by God's people during the post-exilic period. His role highlights the political resistance encountered in fulfilling God's promise to restore worship in Jerusalem. This opposition underscores the faithfulness required by the Israelites to continue their work despite worldly obstacles.
